objective:
Continue the existing goal: rewrite the complete Chromium networking stack in Rust, preserving functionality, compatibility, safety and the existing performance requirements. Preserve the existing goal identity and accounting; do not create a replacement goal or treat a smaller batch as whole-goal completion.

Optimize delivery around whole connected subsystems, not individual functions or small classes. Eight implementation agents work as four exclusive-ownership pairs on HTTP/2 streams/sessions, DNS resolver orchestration/transactions, connection establishment, and cookie storage. Two delivery agents prepare shared interfaces, original-reference dependencies, GN integration and consumer rebuilds. Follow docs/rust/net-subsystem-batches.json and extend dependency-ordered coverage until the entire networking scope is done.

Draft all related policy and control flow for an assigned subsystem together. Prefer reusable safe Rust-to-Rust paths and progressively retire redundant bridges. Preserve independent original C++ algorithms and helper dependencies. Prepare ordinary tests and benchmark workloads alongside code. Use small contract/compiler checks only at meaningful draft milestones; do not interrupt each function or class with a rebuild, extensive test run or benchmark cycle.

At a stable subsystem milestone, integrate the complete production path, batch shared interface changes, build affected targets and consumers, and run regular compatibility, boundary, lifetime, reentry and cancellation tests. Keep configurations stable and one parent-controlled configured writer; coordinate compiler resources. Use source-bound immutable snapshots for longer validation. Broader networking and Chrome checks occur at coordinated milestones and final completion. Sanitizer/fuzz campaigns and security-focused side work remain off under the user's explicit standing override; unperformed checks are recorded as deferred, never as passed.

After subsystem integration and its required regular checks, benchmark complete execution paths in a quiet window, retaining all existing microbenchmarks, cases and history. Archive every run and track every regression. Optimize demonstrated bottlenecks; bridge presence alone proves neither a cause nor a hard blocker. Do not start a new small measurement cycle after each leaf change.

Keep the benchmark page unchanged until the existing publication gate is satisfied. Preserve every pending measurement and accepted or temporary regression. Nothing in the larger-batch workflow waives final correctness, compatibility or performance acceptance. Report draft implementation, compiled integration, correctness validation, performance acceptance and publication separately. Track actual phase durations, rebuild causes and the critical path. Continue through the whole networking backlog, including remaining native/platform/external-provider seams.
